title: The peopling of the Caribbean, c. 4000 BC – AD 1000
summary: People reached Cuba and Hispaniola some six thousand years ago, from Central or South America; which is argued. Saladoid potters came up the Lesser Antilles from the Orinoco from about 500 BC and settled Puerto Rico, and their Taíno descendants spread through the Greater Antilles. The Lucayans crossed to the Bahamas from Hispaniola and Cuba by about AD 800, the people Columbus met in 1492.

legs.source: Taíno (Wikipedia): early Archaic settlers of the Greater Antilles
legs.doubt: Whether the first islanders came from Yucatán and Central America, or from northern South America, is open; the line is one of the options.

legs.source: Saladoid culture (Wikipedia): up the Lesser Antilles from the Orinoco
Taíno (Wikipedia): the Ostionoid and Taíno spread across the Greater Antilles
Lucayan (Wikipedia): the Bahamas settled from Hispaniola and Cuba

events.label: Across the Yucatán Channel
events.text: The earliest firm sites in Cuba and Hispaniola are of hunters and gatherers; their mainland origin is not settled.

events.label: The Orinoco: the Saladoid potters
events.text: People of the lower Orinoco who grew manioc and made white-on-red painted pottery sailed north in dugout canoes, island by island, in a few centuries.

events.label: Puerto Rico
events.text: Saladoid villages appear in Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands. Their culture developed into that of the Taíno over the following centuries.

events.label: The Bahamas: the Lucayans
events.text: The Lucayans settled the Bahamas and lived there about seven centuries, until their enslavement by the Spanish in the early sixteenth century emptied the islands.
